**PCA preserves variation, even when that variation has nothing to do with the label.** Construct two classes spread widely left-to-right. For both, let x1 have variance 100. Put one class near x2=+1 and the other near x2=-1, with very small vertical noise. The classes are easy to separate vertically but look identical horizontally. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/decomposition.html)

The largest total variance is along x1, so one-component PCA retains the horizontal direction and discards x2. In that one-dimensional representation, the class distributions overlap completely. PCA did exactly what it was designed to do: preserve the direction of greatest variance and reduce reconstruction error. It was not optimizing classification.

**LDA uses the labels to choose a different objective.** It seeks large separation of class means relative to within-class spread. Horizontal means are similar and within-class spread is large; vertical means differ and within-class spread is small. The vertical direction therefore has a strong discriminant ratio.

LDA has limits too: estimates can be unstable with little data or singular within-class covariance, and one linear projection may miss nonlinear class structure. Fit PCA or LDA inside the training fold; fitting supervised LDA using test labels leaks the answer. The example shows why dimensionality reduction must match the downstream objective.

**Technical details and references.**

Construct balanced classes with $x_1\sim N(0,100)$ independent of class and $x_2=+1+\epsilon$ for one class, $-1+\epsilon$ for the other, with small noise. The largest variance lies along $x_1$, so one-component PCA discards the nearly perfect class signal in $x_2$. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/decomposition.html)

LDA uses labels and maximizes between-class separation relative to within-class scatter:

$$J(w)=\frac{w^TS_Bw}{w^TS_Ww}.$$

Here it favors the vertical direction. PCA optimizes reconstruction variance, not classification. LDA has its own assumptions and can require regularization when within-class covariance is singular. Fit either transform only on training folds; using test labels for LDA would create direct leakage.
